points.description: Names the two phases of TCP congestion control: slow start and congestion avoidance. Equivalent names are accepted.
Slow start: cwnd increases by one segment for each acknowledgement, so it grows exponentially (roughly doubling each RTT), while cwnd is below ss_thresh. Equivalent wording earns the mark.

Congestion avoidance: once cwnd >= ss_thresh, cwnd grows more slowly, typically linearly (about 1 segment per RTT, or 1 after all outstanding segments are acknowledged). Equivalent wording and other valid incrementation strategies earn the mark.
On packet loss in either phase, ss_thresh is set to half of the current cwnd (ss_thresh = cwnd/2) and cwnd is reset to 1. Both the ss_thresh update and the cwnd reset must be stated.

rubric.notes: Full marks require naming both phases, describing cwnd growth in slow start (exponential, per acknowledgement) and in congestion avoidance (slower, linear), and stating that on loss ss_thresh becomes cwnd/2 and cwnd resets to 1. Missing either the ss_thresh update or the cwnd reset loses that point's mark, and a wrong growth description loses the corresponding phase mark. Equivalent wording and alternative valid growth strategies earn full credit.
